title: Predict struggles, never simulate students
statement: To anticipate where learners will struggle, have a model predict their difficulties from learner data rather than role-play a struggling student.
example: One relayed finding pairs above 90% accuracy on misconceptions with below 25% problem-solving accuracy in the same model.
detail: A course-evaluation engine in the reading project asks a model to predict where students will struggle, never to simulate them, because making a model behave like a struggling student suppresses the reasoning that accurate prediction needs; it relays a figure of above 90% misconception accuracy alongside below 25% problem-solving accuracy in the same model (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/predictor/README.md`, line 9). It cites population-level prediction at r ≈ 0.72–0.79 across three research groups (He-Yueya et al. 2024, Lu & Wang 2024, Xu et al. 2025) (line 13). The model never role-plays a student, and numbers such as learning-model estimates are meant to come in as data from learner profiles (lines 34-35).
against: The figures are relayed second-hand from a BrainLift, with no links to the studies, and the engine is a scaffold that does not validate itself, with a synthetic placeholder in place of real learner profiles: its outputs must be checked against real student outcomes before they are trusted (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/predictor/README.md`, lines 37 and 53-57). Scripted readers that play a stuck learner, kept in another record, do a different job: exercising every branch of a lesson, not predicting difficulty.

evidence.quote: The **Student Data Paradox**: making an LLM behave like a struggling student requires suppressing the reasoning capability you need for accurate prediction. >90% misconception accuracy correlates with <25% problem-solving accuracy in the same model.
reaches r ≈ 0.72–0.79 population-level prediction across three independent research groups (He-Yueya et al. 2024, Lu & Wang 2024, Xu et al. 2025)
It does not simulate student response sequences. The LLM never role-plays as a student.
Those numbers come from the student profiles as input data.
It does not validate itself. Outputs MUST be validated against real student outcomes data before they're trusted (Phase 6 in the build plan).
